title: 472. The Road to The Great War: Britain's Fateful Choice (Part 4)

sentences.en: The discussion had reached its inconclusive end, and the cabinet was about to separate when the quiet, grave tones of Sir Edward Grey's voice were heard,
sentences.zh: 讨论已经迎来了没有结果的尾声，内阁正准备散去，这时爱德华·格雷爵士用平静而低沉的语调开口了，

sentences.en: reading a document which had just been brought to him from the Foreign Office.
sentences.zh: 宣读了一份刚刚从外交部送达他的文件。

sentences.en: It was the Austrian note of Serbia.
sentences.zh: 那是奥地利给塞尔维亚的通牒。

sentences.en: We were all very tired, but gradually, as the phrases and sentences followed one another, impressions of a wholly different character began to form in my mind.
sentences.zh: 我们当时都很疲惫，但随着这些短语和句子一句接一句地念下来，一种截然不同的印象渐渐在我的脑海中成形。

sentences.en: This note was clearly an ultimatum, but it was an ultimatum such as had never been penned in modern times.
sentences.zh: 这份通牒显然是一份最后通牒，但它是一份在现代前所未见的最后通牒。

sentences.en: As the reading proceeded, it seemed absolutely impossible that any state in the world could accept it, or that any acceptance, however abject, would satisfy the aggressor.
sentences.zh: 随着宣读的进行，世上似乎绝没有任何国家能够接受它，也绝没有任何接受方式——无论多么卑躬屈膝——能让侵略者满意。

sentences.zh: 在欧洲地图上浮现并放大。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.zh: 宣读奥地利对塞尔维亚最后通牒的那一刻。

sentences.zh: 听过我们上一期节目的朋友们知道，我们当时是以全世界屏息以待作为结束的。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.zh: 当时人们正等待塞尔维亚对这份非常、非常严厉且苛刻的奥地利最后通牒作出回应。

sentences.zh: 它拥有世界上遥遥领先的最伟大海军，但至关重要的是，它的陆军规模非常、非常小。

sentences.en: So, although the British army have fought battles in the previous decades, they have generally been against, you know, Zulus, Burrs, Afghans, Sudanese, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管英军在过去的几十年里打过仗，但他们通常是对付……你知道的，祖鲁人、布尔人、阿富汗人、苏丹人等等。

sentences.zh: 但由于对布尔人的战争，他们确实换上了卡其色军服，不是吗？

sentences.en: And there's a sense in which, actually, the British probably have fought more wars than most continental powers.
sentences.zh: 某种意义上，事实上英国人打的仗可能比大多数欧洲大陆列强还要多。

sentences.en: They have, but they've been little wars.
sentences.zh: 他们确实打过，但那都是小战争。

sentences.zh: 它们只是治安行动。

sentences.en: They've involved quite small numbers of people.
sentences.zh: 涉及的人数相当少。

sentences.zh: 卡斯特式的军事行动。

sentences.en: Exactly, Custer-esque.
sentences.zh: 没错，卡斯特式的。

sentences.en: Now, Britain, historically, had had alliances.
sentences.zh: 历史上的英国其实有过盟友。

sentences.en: It's not quite right to say that Britain had always stood alone.
sentences.zh: 说英国一直孤军奋战并不完全准确。

sentences.en: So, you know, the Napoleonic Wars, for example, Britain had been part of lots of different coalitions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，比如在拿破仑战争中，英国曾是许多不同反法同盟的一部分。

sentences.en: And the way that British foreign policy had usually worked was that Britain relied on its navy.
sentences.zh: 英国外交政策通常的运作方式是依靠海军。

sentences.en: It had a small army, and it basically paid other people to do the fighting.
sentences.zh: 它只有一支小规模的陆军，基本上是花钱雇别人去打仗。

sentences.en: So, obviously, the Prussians, for example, against Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 显然，比如普鲁士人，就是用来对抗拿破仑的。

sentences.en: And in the Seven Years' War as well.
sentences.zh: 在七年战争中也是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly, in the Seven Years' War.
sentences.zh: 没错，在七年战争中。

sentences.en: But recently, Britain has had this policy of so-called splendid isolation.
sentences.zh: 但近来，英国采取了所谓“光荣孤立”的政策。

sentences.en: So, Lord Salisbury, who was Prime Minister at the turn of the 20th century, had said our policy was to float lazily downstream, putting out the occasional diplomatic boat hook.
sentences.zh: 因此，在20世纪之交担任首相的索尔兹伯里勋爵曾说过，我们的政策就是懒洋洋地顺流而下，偶尔伸出一根外交的船钩。

sentences.en: Great days, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 好日子，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Great days.
sentences.zh: 好日子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I like the sort of wind in the willows analogy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种《柳林风声》式的比喻。

sentences.en: Yeah, with a picnic hamper.
sentences.zh: 对，还带着野餐篮。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But actually, round about the time of the Boer War, which didn't go terribly well for Britain at first, there was a sort of sense, well, actually, we've missed a trick here.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，大约在布尔战争前后，这场战争对英国来说起初并不太顺利，当时人们有一种感觉：好吧，其实我们在这一点上失算/漏掉了关键。

sentences.en: We're fighting fires on lots of different fronts in the colonies, and we don't really have any friends.
sentences.zh: 我们在殖民地的许多不同前线四处救火，而且我们其实没有任何真正的朋友。

sentences.en: So, Joseph Chamberlain, colonial secretary, had said, we have no allies.
sentences.zh: 因此，殖民地大臣约瑟夫·张伯伦曾说过，我们没有盟友。

sentences.en: We have no friends.
sentences.zh: 我们没有朋友。

sentences.en: We stand alone.
sentences.zh: 我们孤立无援。

sentences.en: And he had wanted an alliance with Germany and had got no joy out of it.
sentences.zh: 他曾希望能与德国结盟，但未能如愿。

sentences.zh: 所以最终，英国在1904年与法国签署或达成了《挚诚协定》。

sentences.en: Which is a seismic change, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个翻天覆地的变化，不是吗？

sentences.en: A massive change.
sentences.zh: 巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Because we've said how previously, basically, all these wars are being fought against France, and Britain's continental ally is Prussia, a German state.
sentences.zh: 因为我们之前说过，基本上所有这些战争都是针对法国打的，而英国在欧洲大陆的盟友是普鲁士——一个德国国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And now it's kind of veering around the other way.
sentences.zh: 而现在，风向有点转过来了。

sentences.en: And now Britain has switched horses.
sentences.zh: 现在英国换了阵营。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, is that because Britain has a sense that you should always ally with a lesser power against the most threatening power on the continent?
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，这是因为英国有一种观念：认为永远应该联合一个较弱的势力，去对抗欧洲大陆上最具威胁的势力吗？

sentences.en: And is there a sense now that Germany has become what France used to be, and so the roles have switched?
sentences.zh: 现在是不是有一种感觉，即德国已经成了过去法国扮演的角色，所以双方的角色对调了？

sentences.en: I think that's a huge part of it, that Britain has always wanted to ensure that the continent is not dominated by a single power.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是其中非常大的一部分，英国一直希望确保欧洲大陆不会被单一势力所主导。

sentences.en: So, it makes sense that you ally with somebody a tier down, as it were, against the kind of the top power on the continent.
sentences.zh: 因此，与处于次要地位的某个国家结盟，去对抗欧洲大陆上的顶级强权，这就说得通了。

sentences.en: But also, as with the subsequent convention that we signed with Russia in 1907,
sentences.zh: 但同时，正如我们在1907年与俄国随後签署的公约一样，

sentences.en: we will ally with those countries with whom we are most likely to have friction, to basically dampen down the friction on our colonial frontiers.
sentences.zh: 我们将与那些最容易与我们发生摩擦的国家结盟，以便从根本上平息我们殖民地边境上的摩擦。

sentences.en: So, with France, for example, there had been a war scare.
sentences.zh: 所以，以法国为例，曾发生过战争恐慌。

sentences.en: As recently as 1898, in the Sudan, the so-called Fashoda, or Fashoda, I don't know how you pronounce it actually,
sentences.zh: 就在1898年的苏丹，所谓的法绍达（或者法绍达事件，我其实不知道该怎么发音），

sentences.en: because I've never been and never spoken to any Sudanese person about this incident.
sentences.zh: 因为我从来没去过那里，也从未和任何苏丹人谈起过这件事。

sentences.en: So, this is a mystery to me.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说是个谜。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何。

sentences.en: Well, if we have any Sudanese listeners, let us know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们有任何苏丹听众，请让我们知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 所以，基奇纳和一个法国人基本上从不同方向行军，抵达了这个地方。

sentences.zh: 法国人寡不敌众，并且受到了一些羞辱。

sentences.zh: 这事闹得很大，他们希望避免这种情况再次发生。

sentences.zh: 当然，他们特别希望避免与俄国发生这种情况。

sentences.zh: 为了印度，对吧？

sentences.zh: 皇冠上的明珠。

sentences.zh: 人们担心俄国军队会打进印度。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That this is a great way of managing that.
sentences.zh: 这是管理这种局面的好办法。

sentences.en: That if you actually sign an alliance with them, then, you know, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的与他们签署了同盟条约，那么，你知道的，那就没问题了。

sentences.en: India is protected.
sentences.zh: 印度就安全了。

sentences.zh: 对法国在非洲、东南亚或任何其他地方也是如此。

sentences.zh: 实际上，外交部的大人物们非常明确地表达了这一点。

sentences.zh: 1909年有个叫查尔斯·哈丁的人。

sentences.zh: 他写了一份备忘录。

sentences.zh: 他说，为什么我们要与对我们来说完全不够契合的俄国结盟，而不是像许多人认为的那样，与似乎很契合的德国结盟呢？

sentences.en: So that doesn't necessarily translate into anti-German feeling, does it?
sentences.zh: 所以这并不一定转化为反德情绪，对吧？

sentences.en: And yet, as we've often talked on this podcast, there is a kind of anti-German mood abroad in England at that time.
sentences.zh: 然而，正如我们在这个播客中经常谈到的那样，当时英国国内弥漫着一种反德情绪。

sentences.en: There are all those kind of books about the Battle of the Dorking Gap.
sentences.zh: 到处都是关于《道金斯峡谷战役》之类的小说。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When William came.
sentences.zh: 当威廉来的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's kind of scare stories about a German conquest of Britain.
sentences.zh: 这是一种关于德国征服英国的恐慌故事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Uniquely after the Franco-Prussian War.
sentences.zh: 特别是在普法战争之后。

sentences.en: So those hadn't existed really before.
sentences.zh: 所以这些在以前其实并不存在。

sentences.en: But after Germany is created in 1870, you're absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但自从1870年德国建立之后，你说得完全对，汤姆。

sentences.en: You get this sort of growing anxiety about Germany.
sentences.zh: 你开始感受到这种对德国日益增长的焦虑。

sentences.en: And it really, really starts to kick in, I think, round about the very late end of the 1890s.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，大约在19世纪90年代的超末期，这种情绪真的开始全面爆发了。

sentences.en: The Burr War.
sentences.zh: 布尔战争。

sentences.en: You know, we're fighting Burrs who are not so dissimilar from Germans.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们在和布尔人作战，他们和德国人并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: Well, the Germans, I mean, the Kaiser famously sends supportive telegrams, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 德国人，我是说，威廉二世不是很有名地发过支持电报吗？

sentences.en: He does, the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 是的，威廉二世。

sentences.en: And in fact, lots of Germans, and frankly, lots of other people around the world, say the plucky Burr underdogs and these bullying shopkeeper, you know, the British.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多德国人，坦白说，还有世界上许多其他人，都认为勇敢的布尔人是弱者，而这些霸道的店小二，你知道的，就是英国人。

sentences.en: With a butcher's apron.
sentences.zh: 带着一块屠夫的围裙。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of stuff about that.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多关于这方面的内容。

sentences.en: There are all those, as you said, I mean, I love all that invasion scare stuff.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，有所有这些，我是说，我喜欢所有那些关于遭到入侵的恐慌内容。

sentences.en: It'd be brilliant subjects, actually, for a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这会是播客的绝佳主题。

sentences.en: Really whipped up by the Northcliffe newspapers.
sentences.zh: 确实是被诺思克利夫的报纸给煽动起来的。

sentences.en: So my old stamping grounds, the Daily Mail, very prominent in that.
sentences.zh: 所以我的老地盘《每日邮报》，在这方面非常显眼。

sentences.en: Because basically they would publish scare stories in places where their circulation was low.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上他们会在自己发行量低的地方发布耸人听闻的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, then what they did was the key battles took place in places where they had lots of readers.
sentences.zh: 好吧，然后他们所做的是，关键战役都发生在他们有很多读者的那些地方。

sentences.en: Because to terrify, you know, Watford sacked by the Prussians or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为为了制造恐慌，你知道的，比如普鲁士人洗劫沃特福德之类的。

sentences.en: And then the other thing is the naval race.
sentences.zh: 然后另一件事就是海军军备竞赛。

sentences.en: Once the German Empire is established, and then once it sort of got going, they decide they'd like a fleet.
sentences.zh: 一旦德意志帝国建立起来，并且一旦它运转起来，他们就决定想要一支舰队。

sentences.en: A fleet is seen in the 1890s as really the supreme badge.
sentences.zh: 在1890年代，舰队被视为真正的最高标志。

sentences.en: It's like having nuclear weapons or something.
sentences.zh: 就像拥有核武器或者别的什么。

sentences.en: This is your ticket to the top table.
sentences.zh: 这是你进入最高决策层的入场券。

sentences.en: The British are very offended by this.
sentences.zh: 英国人对此感到非常被冒犯。

sentences.en: They start building dreadnoughts.
sentences.zh: 他们开始建造无畏舰。

sentences.en: And this creates a lot of antagonism.
sentences.zh: 这造成了大量的对立情绪。

sentences.en: But actually, Britain wins that naval race hands down.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，英国人轻而易举地赢得了那场海军竞赛。

sentences.en: By 1913, the Germans have unilaterally declared, it's over.
sentences.zh: 到了1913年，德国人单方面宣布，结束了。

sentences.en: We can't compete.
sentences.zh: 我们竞争不过。

sentences.en: We're not going to carry on building dreadnoughts at the same rate.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算以同样的速率继续建造无畏舰了。

sentences.en: You know, fine.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，好吧。

sentences.en: Have your naval advantage.
sentences.zh: 你们保留你们的海军优势吧。

sentences.en: So that actually means that as you get to 1914, the temperature is a little bit lower than it had been.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上意味着，当你进入1914年时，紧张气氛比之前要稍微缓和了一些。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So we've already mentioned it, that trip to Berlin by Haldane, Richard Haldane.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经提到过了，霍尔丹，理查德·霍尔丹对柏林的访问。

sentences.en: Yeah, the war minister.
sentences.zh: 对，陆军大臣。

sentences.en: The war minister to try and kind of form a German equivalent of the Entente Cordiale.
sentences.zh: 陆军大臣试图建立一种德版的英法协约。

sentences.en: I mean, it fails.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这失败了。

sentences.en: But presumably, it's a sign that actually relations between them are thawing.
sentences.zh: 但据推测，这表明他们之间的关系实际上正在融冰。

sentences.en: Yes, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也这么认为。

sentences.en: I mean, because on the kind of personal level, there are lots of people in the British upper classes who are very, very keen on Germany to a degree that is, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是说，因为在某种个人层面，英国上流社会有很多人非常非常热衷于德国，达到了一种，你知道的，

sentences.en: is not comparable today.
sentences.zh: 是今天是无法比拟的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People have been massively influenced by German culture for an entire century, going back to the time of Coleridge, you know, George Eliot, all those kind of intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 整整一个世纪以来，人们都深受德国文化的影响，追溯到柯勒律治的时代，你知道的，乔治·艾略特，所有那些知识分子。

sentences.en: Hugely influenced by Germany in a way that would be inconceivable today.
sentences.zh: 深受德国影响，这种程度在今天是不可想象的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you could reasonably argue that if there was a point in recent in modern British history when people were most keen on Germany and German culture,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为你可以合理地争辩说，如果在近代英国历史上有那么一个时期，人们对德国和德国文化最热情的话，

sentences.en: it was actually in the 1900s and 1910s.
sentences.zh: 实际上就是在20世纪0年代和10年代。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so ironic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，这太讽刺了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And it went both ways.
sentences.zh: 而且这是双向的。

sentences.en: So the man who had masterminded the naval race for the Germans, Grand Admiral Tirpitz, he had an English governess for his daughters,
sentences.zh: 所以，为德国人精心策划了海军竞赛的那个人，大海军上将蒂尔皮茨，他的女儿们请了一位英国家庭教师，

sentences.en: and then he sent his daughters to Cheltenham Lader's College because he wanted them to have an English education.
sentences.zh: 然后他把女儿们送到切尔滕纳姆女子学院，因为他想让她们接受英国教育。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: So even in that cabinet, in that meeting that you described so beautifully with your Churchill voice, Sir John Simon, who's one of the liberal cabinet ministers,
sentences.zh: 所以甚至在那届内阁中，在你用丘胺的嗓音美妙描述的那场会议上，西里尔·约翰·西蒙，他是自由党内阁大臣之一，

sentences.en: he had said publicly, the fellow countrymen of Shakespeare and Milton cannot look askance on the fellow countrymen of Goethe and Schiller,
sentences.zh: 他曾公开表示，莎士比亚和弥尔顿的同胞不能斜眼看待歌德和席勒的同胞，

sentences.en: and those with the tradition of Wycliffe and Wesley have no ground of quarrel with the descendants of Luther.
sentences.zh: 而拥有威克利夫和卫斯理传统的人与路德的后代没有任何争吵的理由。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: There's the famous German joke about Shakespeare, isn't it, that the English translation of Shakespeare isn't bad.
sentences.zh: 关于莎士比亚，有一个著名的德国笑话，不是吗，就是莎士比亚的英文翻译还不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, the Germans absolutely adore and look up to British high culture.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，德国人绝对崇拜并仰慕英国的高等文化。

sentences.en: There's no question about that.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: So you have that.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Now, you do have people in the Foreign Office who are very down on Germany, and we'll get into one of them a little bit later in the story.
sentences.zh: 现在，外交部里确实有些人非常看低德国，我们稍后会在故事中深入探讨其中一人。

sentences.en: But Christopher Clarke talks about this in The Sleepwalkers.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯托弗·克拉克在《梦游者》中谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: He says there's a steady stream of memos and minutes arguing about the threat posed by Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他说，有一连串源源不断的备忘录和会议记录，都在争论柏林构成的威胁。

sentences.en: And he has a lovely analogy, which I think could be developed even further.
sentences.zh: 他有一个极好的比喻，我认为还可以进一步阐发。

sentences.en: He says all of these people, they read those kind of Edwardian stories in which there's a new boy at the school.
sentences.zh: 他说所有这些人，他们读那种爱德华时代的的故事，里面学校里来了一个新男孩。

sentences.en: You know, he's maybe a bit vulgar.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他可能有点粗俗。

sentences.en: New money.
sentences.zh: 暴发户。

sentences.en: Yeah, new money.
sentences.zh: 对，暴发户。

sentences.en: He comes from new money, and he's a bit of a braggart, and he's a blusterer.
sentences.zh: 他来自暴发户家庭，而且有点爱吹牛，是个虚张声势的人。

sentences.en: And the older boys sort of punish him and tame him.
sentences.zh: 年长的男孩们会有点惩罚他、驯服他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's not familiar with the traditional rules of the school.
sentences.zh: 他不熟悉学校的传统规则。

sentences.en: I mean, he says, this is how Foreign Office Mandarin's talked about Germany.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他说，这就是外交部高级官员谈论德国的方式。

sentences.en: And of course, this, by the way, is how Kaiser Wilhelm's relatives talk about him.
sentences.zh: 当然，顺便说一句，这也是威廉皇帝的亲戚们谈论他的方式。

sentences.en: But the Kaiser undoubtedly has a feeling that he's been treated a bit like that.
sentences.zh: 但威廉皇帝无疑有一种感觉，觉得自己被那样对待了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: The new boy who's not being made to feel welcome in the dorm.
sentences.zh: 那个在宿舍里没有受到欢迎的新男孩。

sentences.en: And of course, what gives that an extra charge is that Germany is doing so well.
sentences.zh: 当然，赋予这一点额外张力的是德国发展得太好了。

sentences.en: So that Germany, by the outbreak of the First World War, has overtaken Britain in industrial production.
sentences.zh: 因此，到第一次世界大战爆发时，德国在工业生产上已经超过了英国。

sentences.en: It is right behind Britain in its share of world trade.
sentences.zh: 它在世界贸易份额紧随英国之后。

sentences.en: People are aware of these figures.
sentences.zh: 人们都清楚这些数字。

sentences.en: You know, they have a real sense of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们对此有切身的感受。

sentences.en: People make jokes in the early 20th century about products that are stamped, made in Germany.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初的人们拿印有“德国制造”的产品开玩笑。

sentences.en: And they find that, you know, as unsettling as Americans did in the 1980s and 1990s when it was made in Japan or something.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，你知道的，这就像美国人在20世纪80年代和90年代看到“日本制造”或类似的东西时一样让人感到不安。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So kind of what the Americans would call the Thucydides trap.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是美国人所说的修昔底德陷阱。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The Thucydides trap, exactly.
sentences.zh: 修昔底德陷阱，完全正确。

sentences.en: The rising power must, by definition, challenge.
sentences.zh: 崛起中的大国，按定义就必然会发起挑战。

sentences.en: But do you think that's right?
sentences.zh: 但你觉得这正确吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that it's inevitable that, for instance, Britain would see Germany as an enemy rather than as a potential ally?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是不可避免的吗，比如英国把德国视为敌人，而不是潜在的盟友？

sentences.en: It's inevitable.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Because the implication of what you're saying is that that's not the case at all.
sentences.zh: 因为你所说的话的含义是，情况根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: I don't think it is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: We've already mentioned two different very, very influential British politicians, Joseph Chamberlain and Richard Haldane.
sentences.zh: 我们已经提到过两位非常、非常有影响力的英国政治家，约瑟夫·张伯伦和理查德·霍尔丹。

sentences.en: Huge figures in their day, not maybe household names today, but huge figures in the 1890s, 1900s, who really, really wanted an alliance with Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们在当时是巨头，今天可能不是家喻户晓的名字，但在1890年代、1900年代却是巨头，他们非常、非常渴望与德国结盟。

sentences.en: And I think the general sense, certainly by 1914, is, yeah, we've had spats and arguments and things, but actually things are now getting much better.
sentences.zh: 我认为普遍的看法，当然到1914年时是，是的，我们有过争吵、争论和类似的事情，但实际上现在情况好多了。

sentences.en: So Arthur Nicholson, who's running the foreign office, the top civil servant, says the Germans have been making great efforts to be on the best possible terms with us.
sentences.zh: 所以管理外交部的最高公务员亚瑟·尼科尔森说，德国人一直在做出巨大努力，以便与我们保持尽可能好的关系。

sentences.en: And, you know, to some extent they've succeeded.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在某种程度上他们成功了。

sentences.en: David Lloyd George, the chancellor, gave an interview on New Year's Day in 1914 to the Daily News.
sentences.zh: 财政大臣大卫·劳埃德·乔治在1914年元旦接受了《每日新闻》的采访。

sentences.en: And he said, our relations with Germany are infinitely more friendly now than they have been for years.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们与德国的关系现在比多年来的任何时候都要友好得多。

sentences.en: Now, there'd be some people who believed that point that you make this sort of these traps, some people in the foreign office who would say, realistically,
sentences.zh: 现在，会有些人相信你所表达的观点，也就是这种陷阱，外交部里有些人会现实地认为，

sentences.en: Germany is going to challenge us and we should gird our loins for that.
sentences.zh: 德国将向我们发起挑战，我们应该为此做好准备。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is exactly like the German attitude to Russia.
sentences.zh: 这完全就像德国对俄罗斯的态度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Sooner, better, rather than later.
sentences.zh: 与其夜长梦多，不如早点动手。

sentences.en: But it is much less charged in Britain and much less paranoid.
sentences.zh: 但在英国，这种情绪要少得多，也没有那么偏执。

sentences.en: Well, also because Britain in 1914, I mean, we know this because we did a series on the Easter Rising,
sentences.zh: 嗯，也是因为1914年的英国，我是说，我们知道这一点，因为我们做过一期关于复活节起义的系列节目，

sentences.en: that Britain in 1914 is pretty inward looking because it's wracked by all kinds of crises, of which the Irish debate over home rule is the major one.
sentences.zh: 1914年的英国相当内向，因为它被各种危机所困扰，其中爱尔兰关于地方自治的辩论是主要的一场。

sentences.en: But you've got the suffragettes, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 但你还有女权争取选举权运动的人，对吧？

sentences.en: You've got kind of strikes.
sentences.zh: 你还有各种罢工。

sentences.en: So the sense we tend to have of it being a kind of golden summer bank holiday suddenly that turns to mud and rain isn't entirely true.
sentences.zh: 所以我们往往觉得那是一个黄金般的夏天银行假日，却突然变成泥泞和阴雨的这种印象，并不完全真实。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: There are crises everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是危机。

sentences.en: And I always remember that incredible comment that Asquith makes to the effect that, you know, he says, well, at least the war will distract us from, you know,
sentences.zh: 我总是想起阿斯奎斯说的那句令人难以置信的话大意是，你知道的，他说，至少战争会把我们的注意力从，你知道的，

sentences.en: the horrors of potential civil war in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰潜在内战的恐怖中转移开。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The very day after Franz Ferdinand and Sophie were assassinated in Sarajevo, Sir Henry Wilson from the British Army told Asquith, he said,
sentences.zh: 就在弗朗茨·斐迪南和索菲在萨拉热窝被刺杀的第二天，英国陆军的亨利·威尔逊爵士对阿斯奎斯说，他说，

sentences.en: we're going to have to send the entire army to Ireland to deal with the consequences of home rule.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不把整支军队派往爱尔兰，来应对地方自治带来的后果。

sentences.en: So the British do not have their eyes on the Balkans at all at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个时候，英国人的目光根本没有放在巴尔干半岛上。

sentences.en: Of course, the Sarajevo assassinations were extensively reported in Britain.
sentences.zh: 当然，萨拉热窝的刺杀事件在英国得到了广泛报道。

sentences.en: The Times ran seven different stories on the assassinations the next day.
sentences.zh: 第二天，《泰晤士报》刊登了关于刺杀事件的七篇不同的报道。

sentences.en: And the tone is sympathetic.
sentences.zh: 而且语气是充满同情的。

sentences.en: Totally sympathetic.
sentences.zh: 完全充满同情。

sentences.en: I mean, they're all, gosh, the poor old emperor, Franz Joseph, you know, he's endured so many trials, the death of his wife, the death of his son.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们都在想，天哪，老皇帝弗朗茨·约瑟夫太可怜了，你知道的，他经历了那么多的磨难，妻子的死，儿子的死。

sentences.en: And Franz Ferdinand and Sophie had been visitors in Britain just the year before, hadn't they?
sentences.zh: 而且弗朗茨·斐迪南和索菲就在前一年还访问过英国，不是吗？

sentences.en: And everyone said they were such tremendous people, had actually liked them.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说他们是了不起的人，实际上都很喜欢他们。

sentences.en: So Buckingham Palace is in mourning, there's a big service of remembrance at Westminster Cathedral, the Catholic Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 所以白金汉宫在哀悼，威斯敏斯特大教堂（天主教大教堂）举行了一场盛大的追悼仪式。

sentences.en: And quite a lot of the cabinet went to that service to express their condolences.
sentences.zh: 相当多的内阁成员去参加了那场仪式以表达哀悼。

sentences.en: So there's a natural sympathy.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种天然的同情。

sentences.en: And then there's a sense, well, it's actually not that big a deal, you know, in the grand scheme of things.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一种感觉，嗯，在宏大的事物格局中，这其实并不是什么大不了的事。

sentences.en: So there's a very famous...
sentences.zh: 所以有一个非常著名的……

sentences.en: The Guardian kicks in with very prescient editorial.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》发表了一篇极具先见之明的社论。

sentences.en: Yeah, the murders will have no immediate or salient effect on the politics of Europe.
sentences.zh: 对，这些谋杀案不会对欧洲政治产生直接或显著的影响。

sentences.en: Not the last time the Guardian would comically misjudge world affairs, I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想可以说，这并不是《卫报》最后一次滑稽地误判世界事务，汤姆。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And in fact, in the Foreign Office, the general sense is this will blow over.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在外交部，普遍的看法是这件事会过去的。

sentences.en: You know, this will not be a massive deal.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不会是什么大不了的事。

sentences.en: Now, the one person who is where straight away, you've already described him and said he's a great hero of yours, is the Foreign Secretary,
sentences.zh: 现在，唯一一个立刻意识到情况的人，你已经描述过他并说他是你心目中的伟大英雄，那就是外交大臣，

sentences.en: the man who basically runs foreign policy as a private fiefdom and has done for a decade.
sentences.zh: 那个基本上把外交政策当成私人领地并已经这样做了十年的男人。

sentences.en: And that is Sir Edward Grey.
sentences.zh: 那就是爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: So, Tom, you love Sir Edward Grey.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，你深爱着爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: And what is it about him that appeals to you?
sentences.zh: 他身上有什么特质吸引了你？

sentences.en: He is the embodiment of a certain languid superiority that I would dearly like to possess.
sentences.zh: 他是某种慵懒优越感的化身，而我非常渴望拥有这种优越感。

sentences.en: That you associate with yourself.
sentences.zh: 你把这和自己联系在一起。

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: But I aspire to it.
sentences.zh: 但我渴望拥有它。

sentences.en: So Sir Edward Grey remains to this day an absolutely fated fly fisherman.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华·格雷爵士直到今天仍然是一位绝对命定的飞蝇钓鱼者。

sentences.en: His book on fly fishing is very, very highly regarded.
sentences.zh: 他关于飞蝇钓的书备受推崇。

sentences.en: And you'll know that I'm in the process of trying to take it up.
sentences.zh: 你会知道我正在试图开始这项爱好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I'd like to give a big shout out to Jeff, who I know is a regular listener, who's doing his best to teach me.
sentences.zh: 我想向杰夫大声致意，我知道他是位忠实的听众，他正在尽最大努力教我。

sentences.en: So thank you, Jeff, for all your struggles.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，杰夫，感谢你付出的所有努力。

sentences.en: And basically, when I stand there trying to cast a fly, if I think that it's me who's doing it, it all goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当我站在那里试图抛投拟饵时，如果我觉得这是我在操控，事情就会一团糟。

sentences.en: I get the hook in my finger or the line gets tangled in a tree or I spear a duck or something.
sentences.zh: 我会把鱼钩勾到手指上，或者鱼线缠在树上，或者我不小心戳到了一只鸭子之类的。

sentences.en: But if I imagine myself to be Sir Edward Grey.
sentences.zh: 但如果我把自己想象成爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In fact, I have a Sir Edward Grey hat.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我有一顶爱德华·格雷爵士同款帽子。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Which I wear.
sentences.zh: 我戴着的这顶。

sentences.en: You're going to wear it now?
sentences.zh: 你现在就要把它戴上吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: So people are watching this on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以大家正在YouTube上看着这一切。

sentences.en: I'm now going to put it on.
sentences.zh: 我现在要把它戴上了。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这真的太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's a wonderful hat.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一顶好帽子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I got it from Sir Edward Grey's outfitter.
sentences.zh: 我是从爱德华·格雷爵士的定制店买的。

sentences.en: So it's exactly the same one.
sentences.zh: 所以完全是一模一样的。

sentences.en: And I imagine myself as Sir Edward Grey in the summer of 1914 casting.
sentences.zh: 然后我把自己想象成1914年夏天正在抛投的爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: And then I can do it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 接着我就能完美地完成动作了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I think that's the measure of the man.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这就是这个人的水平。

sentences.en: Lesson of all aspiring fishermen there.
sentences.zh: 所有有志成为钓鱼者之人的前车之鉴。

sentences.en: So Sir Edward Grey came from a Whig family.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·格雷爵士来自一个辉格党家庭。

sentences.en: I mean, you say that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't just come from a Whig family.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他可不仅仅是来自一个辉格党家庭。

sentences.en: It's a Whig dynasty, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个辉格党王朝，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Whig dynasty.
sentences.zh: 对，辉格党王朝。

sentences.en: He's the great-grandnephew of the Earl Grey who introduces the Great Reform Act in 1832.
sentences.zh: 他是格雷伯爵的曾孙侄，正是那位伯爵在1832年推出了《伟大改革法案》。

sentences.en: But much more significantly.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的。

sentences.en: And the reason why he's remembered gives his name to the eponymous T.
sentences.zh: 他之所以被人铭记并以他的名字命名了一种同名茶。

sentences.en: Is that named after the Earl Grey?
sentences.zh: 那是用格雷伯爵的名字命名的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我以前不知道。

sentences.en: I'm not a massive fan of...
sentences.zh: 我不是特别喜欢……

sentences.en: I don't like a scented T.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢加了香精的茶。

sentences.en: But it's very liberal, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这非常自由主义，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's too liberal.
sentences.zh: 对，太自由主义了。

sentences.en: So Edward Grey, you know, high-born, goes to Winchester College, one of the great schools that we talked about in our The Real Hogwarts podcasts.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华·格雷，你知道的，出身名门，就读于温彻斯特公学，也就是我们在播客《真正的霍格沃茨》里聊过的那些伟大名校之一。

sentences.en: Then he went to Balliol College, Oxford, like his great friend, Herbert Henry Asquith.
sentences.zh: 后来他去了牛津大学贝利奥尔学院，就像他的好朋友赫伯特·亨利·阿斯奎斯一样。

sentences.en: And indeed you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 还有你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And indeed me, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实还有我，是的。

sentences.en: And unlike me, he had a life of pure pleasure.
sentences.zh: 但与我不同的是，他过着纯粹享乐的生活。

sentences.en: I was a bookworm, Tom, I'm sorry to say.
sentences.zh: 我以前是个书呆子，汤姆，遗憾的是。

sentences.en: Didn't you play football for Balliol?
sentences.zh: 你没有为贝利奥尔学院踢过足球吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我踢过。

sentences.en: Grey played football for Balliol.
sentences.zh: 格雷曾为贝利奥尔学院踢过足球。

sentences.en: Did he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Probably at a higher level than I did, Tom.
sentences.zh: 水平可能比我高，汤姆。

sentences.en: Maybe, but I mean...
sentences.zh: 也许吧，但我的意思是……

sentences.en: That's yet another resonance with this podcast, right?
sentences.zh: 这又与本播客产生了一个共鸣，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he was actually sent down, which I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 所以他实际上被勒令退学了，而我没有。

sentences.en: He was sent down for not doing any work.
sentences.zh: 他因为不干活而被勒令退学。

sentences.en: The College Minute Book said he'd been admonished for idleness and shown himself entirely ignorant of the work set for him in the vacation.
sentences.zh: 学院会议记录说他因懒散受到训诫，并表现出对假期布置的功课一无所知。

sentences.en: So that's bad form.
sentences.zh: 这行为可真够糟糕的。

sentences.en: But that doesn't stop him becoming Liberal MP for a place very close to my heart.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止他成为一个对我来说有着特殊感情地方的自由党议员。

sentences.en: For Berwick!
sentences.zh: 为了贝里克！

sentences.en: Where I have my Scottish estate.
sentences.zh: 我在那里有苏格兰庄园。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, it has excellent fishing, obviously, on the Tweed.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，那里的特威德河显然有着极佳的垂钓条件。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also a lot of squirrels.
sentences.zh: 而且还有很多松鼠。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 那挺不错的。

sentences.en: A lot of red squirrels.
sentences.zh: 有很多红松鼠。

sentences.en: So we've seen red squirrels up near our Scottish estate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在苏格兰庄园附近见过红松鼠。

sentences.en: This is really spiralling off now, this story of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 这个关于第一次世界大战的故事现在真的扯远了。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: But so his base is north of Northumbria, a place called Faladon.
sentences.zh: 但他的基地在诺森伯兰郡以北，一个叫法拉登的地方。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's so devoted to squirrels that Lloyd George suggested that if the Germans invaded and were marching on the northeaSt...
sentences.zh: 他对松鼠如此痴迷，以至于劳合·乔治曾建议说，如果德国人入侵并向东北部进军……

sentences.en: Yes, I remember that.
sentences.zh: 对，我记得那个。

sentences.en: ...then he could be made to yield by, you know, a German captain who threatened to exterminate the squirrels around his house at Faladon.
sentences.zh: ……那么可以通过让一个德国指挥官威胁要消灭他在法拉登家周围的松鼠，来迫使他屈服。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I really like that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这个。

sentences.en: So he spends a lot of time in these country pursuits, I think partly because his private life is a bit of a mess.
sentences.zh: 所以他花了很多时间在这些乡村爱好上，我想部分原因是因为他的私生活一团糟。

sentences.en: Not a mess, it's just a bit of a wasteland.
sentences.zh: 不是一团糟，只是有点像一片荒漠。

sentences.en: So he married a young woman called Dorothy from a big Northumberland land-owning family.
sentences.zh: 所以他娶了一个名叫多萝西的年轻女子，她来自诺森伯兰郡一个拥有大片土地的家族。

sentences.en: They went on honeymoon and Dorothy said to him at the end of the honeymoon,
sentences.zh: 他们去度蜜月，蜜月结束时多萝西对他说，

sentences.en: I actually find the physical side of marriage repulsive, which is...
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得婚姻中身体上的接触令人反感，这……

sentences.en: No one wants to hear that.
sentences.zh: 没人想听到这个。

sentences.en: You don't want to hear that from your new bride.
sentences.zh: 你可不想从新婚妻子那里听到这话。

sentences.en: So that side of the marriage was then dead.
sentences.zh: 所以他们婚姻的那个方面就名存实亡了。

sentences.en: And his biographer, Tomasotti, says he took up competitive real tennis with greater energy.
sentences.zh: 他的传记作家托马索蒂说，他以更大的热情投入到了竞技皇家网球中。

sentences.en: Well, that's the solution.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这倒是个解决办法。

sentences.en: So real tennis is the one where you have a kind of very heavy ball, don't you?
sentences.zh: 皇家网球就是那种用一种非常重的球的网球，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's kind of modelled on a medieval monastery or something.
sentences.zh: 它的设计似乎是模仿中世纪修道院之类的。

sentences.en: It's quite dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这相当危险。

sentences.en: But he's really good at it.
sentences.zh: 但他真的很擅长。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I think he got a blue.
sentences.zh: 我想他拿过牛津剑桥校际运动蓝带奖。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think he was exceptionally good.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得他极其优秀。

sentences.en: And he played squash and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他还打壁球以及诸如此类的各种运动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He won all kinds of national championships.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了各种全国锦标赛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's doing that and he spends all his weekends fly fishing and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他一边做这些，一边把所有的周末都花在飞蝇钓鱼之类的活动上。

sentences.en: And in fact, somebody at the foreign office said, he's never been abroad or hardly ever.
sentences.zh: 事实上，外交部曾有人说，他从来没去过国外，或者几乎没去过。

sentences.en: Doesn't speak French, does he?
sentences.zh: 不会说法语，对吧？

sentences.en: Doesn't speak a word of any foreign languages.
sentences.zh: 连一句外语都不会说。

sentences.en: It would be advisable for him to spare some time from his ducks to learn French.
sentences.zh: 建议他从鸭子身上分出一些时间来学学法语。

sentences.en: But Grey obviously thinks that's not suitable for a Balliol man to do that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但格雷显然认为，对于一个贝利奥尔学院的人来说，做这种事不太合适。

sentences.en: I just love the idea of him, you know, of a weekend, Friday evening, he gets on the train, goes down and fishes.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢他那种形象，你知道的，周末的时候，周五晚上，他坐上火车，下去钓鱼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That for me, I mean, basically, that's how I like to imagine the Edwardian period.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，基本上，我就是喜欢这样想象爱德华时代。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I know all about, you know, strikes and Ireland and everything.
sentences.zh: 我知道关于罢工、爱尔兰以及一切的事情。

sentences.en: But the image of a man in tweed with a hat fly fishing on a lazy June afternoon.
sentences.zh: 但在一个慵懒的六月午后，一个穿着呢子衣、戴着帽子的男人在河边进行飞蝇钓鱼的画面。

sentences.en: Having just spent the day settling the affairs of Montenegro.
sentences.zh: 当时他刚刚花了一整天时间来平息黑山的事态。

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or whatever he's been doing.
sentences.zh: 或者不管他一直在忙什么。

sentences.en: But the thing is, he fishes in a very melancholy way, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他钓鱼的方式非常忧郁，汤姆。

sentences.en: Dorothy died in 1906 in a riding accident.
sentences.zh: 多萝西于1906年在一次骑马事故中去世了。

sentences.en: And Grey, he always reminds me of Thomas Hardy in this regard, who obviously is living at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而格雷在这方面总是让我想起托马斯·哈代，他显然是同时代的人。

sentences.en: Thomas Hardy, when he lost his first wife, wrote all these sort of poems saying, you know, we didn't really get on and I feel so guilty.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·哈代在失去第一任妻子时，写了各种各样的诗，说什么，你知道的，我们其实合不来，我感到很内疚。

sentences.en: The clouds have gathered and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 乌云密布以及诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: And Grey, absolutely, he is ravaged by a sort of strange guilt after her death.
sentences.zh: 而格雷完全是这样，她在死后被一种奇怪的内疚感折磨得心力交瘁。

sentences.en: So he would have tea laid in her room when he was in your neck of the woods in Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在你那片地盘诺森伯兰郡时，他会让人把茶具摆在她的房间里。

sentences.en: And he would just sit there silently on his own, staring at the tea set.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会独自一人静静地坐在那里，盯着茶具看。

sentences.en: And he said to people, I wish I could be dead.
sentences.zh: 他对别人说，我希望我能死去。

sentences.en: I wish I could join her in death.
sentences.zh: 我希望能在死后陪伴她。

sentences.en: I also like that melancholy strain.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢那种忧郁的调调。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, that's very Edwardian.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那非常具有爱德华时代的特色。

sentences.en: The worst state of all is to feel dead and to have to go on being alive.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的状态莫过于觉得自己已经死了，却还不得不继续活着。

sentences.en: That is my difficulty now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我现在的困境。

sentences.zh: 然后他的兄弟在非洲被狮子杀死了。

sentences.en: Very Edwardian.
sentences.zh: 非常爱德华时代。

sentences.en: And then he starts to lose his sight.
sentences.zh: 接着他的视力开始下降。

sentences.en: And for a man who basically spends all his time playing real tennis and birdwatching.
sentences.zh: 而对于一个基本上把所有时间都花在打皇家网球和观鸟上的人来说。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful photo of him wearing his fisherman's hat with a robin on top of it.
sentences.zh: 有一张非常精彩的照片，他戴着渔夫帽，帽顶上停着一只知更鸟。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And another one, he's sitting on a bench surrounded by ducks.
sentences.zh: 还有一张，他坐长椅上，周围全是鸭子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's a very proficient birdwatcher.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常资深的观鸟者。

sentences.zh: 现在，所有这一切让他听起来，特别是对我们海外的某些人来说，仿佛是一个充满肌肉感力的

sentences.en: Australian listener to the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 来自《历史之趣》的澳大利亚听众。

sentences.en: This will confirm all their stereotypes of the English, right?
sentences.zh: 这会证实他们对英国人的所有刻板印象，对吧？

sentences.en: This sort of languid, useless, don't speak a word of the foreign language, just interested in birdwatching.
sentences.zh: 这种慵懒的、无用的、连一句外语都不会说、只对观鸟感兴趣的形象。

sentences.en: For example, he meets the Russian ambassador, Count von Bekendorf.
sentences.zh: 例如，他会见了俄罗斯大使冯·本肯多夫伯爵。

sentences.en: Everybody has the wrong name.
sentences.zh: 所有人的名字都弄反了。

sentences.en: Lichnowski and Bekendorf should have swapped surnames.
sentences.zh: 利希诺夫斯基和本肯多夫应该交换姓氏。

sentences.en: Bizarrely, I mean, or not bizarrely, given how Edwardian diplomatic politics works.
sentences.zh: 说来奇怪，我的意思是，或者也不算奇怪，考虑到爱德华时代的外交政治是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Bekendorf, the Russian ambassador, and Lichnowski, the German ambassador, are cousins.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯大使本肯多夫和德国大使利希诺夫斯基是表兄弟。

sentences.en: Of course they are.
sentences.zh: 他们当然是。

sentences.en: So he meets him and he says to him, what we should perhaps do is reassure the Germans.
sentences.zh: 所以他与他会面并对他说，我们或许应该做的是安抚德国人。

sentences.en: We don't want the Germans to be too isolated.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让德国人被孤立得太厉害。

sentences.en: We want to reassure them.
sentences.zh: 我们要让他们安心。

sentences.en: You know, he still thinks the Russians, the French, the Germans, indeed the Austrians, they're all solid chaps.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他仍然认为俄国人、法国人、德国人，甚至是奥地利人，他们都是可靠的家伙。

sentences.en: They can all be brought to sea sense.
sentences.zh: 他们都能被劝导回到理智上来。

sentences.en: Of course there are differences between them.
sentences.zh: 他们之间当然存在分歧。

sentences.en: But if I show myself to be a man of good faith, they will all agree to some sort of mediation.
sentences.zh: 但如果我表现得诚心诚意，他们都会同意某种形式的调解。

sentences.en: And as you said, Tom, that's slightly missing the point that he's already promised the French that when it comes to the crunch, he will be on their side.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，汤姆，这有点没有抓住重点，那就是他已经向法国人承诺过，一旦到了紧关头，他会站在他们一边。

sentences.en: So they can kind of ignore him if they want.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们愿意，他们其实可以忽略他。

sentences.en: They don't have to go with his kind of mediation proposals.
sentences.zh: 他们不必接受他那种调解提议。

sentences.en: So right up to the point when the Austrians issue their ultimatum, he is still pretty sympathetic to Austria.
sentences.zh: 因此，直到奥地利人发出最后通牒的那一刻，他对奥地利仍然相当同情。

sentences.en: So the 22nd of July, he meets the Austrian ambassador.
sentences.zh: 所以在7月22日，他会见了奥地利大使。

sentences.en: Like all Austrian ambassadors, he has an enormous name.
sentences.zh: 像所有奥地利大使一样，他有着一个极长的名字。

sentences.en: Count Albert Victor Julius Josef Michael Graf von Mensdorf Puigli Dietrich Stein.
sentences.zh: 阿尔伯特·维克托·尤利乌斯·约瑟夫·米歇尔·冯·门斯多夫-普伊利-迪特里希施泰因伯爵。
zh_words: 阿尔伯特·维克托·尤利乌斯·约瑟夫·米歇尔·冯·门斯多夫

sentences.en: Crazy name.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的名字。

sentences.en: Crazy guy.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的家伙。

sentences.en: We call him Count Mensdorf.
sentences.zh: 我们叫他门斯多夫伯爵。

sentences.en: And Mensdorf reports to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 门斯多夫向维也纳汇报。

sentences.en: He says, Gray is not without sympathy for us.
sentences.zh: 他说，格雷对我们并非毫无同情。

sentences.en: He's very cool.
sentences.zh: 他非常冷静。

sentences.en: He's very friendly.
sentences.zh: 他非常友好。

sentences.en: He is worried about what will happen.
sentences.zh: 他担心会发生什么。

sentences.en: And actually, the ambassador says to Vienna, I am anxious that when Gray sees our ultimatum, he will be really shocked.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这位大使对维也纳说，我担心当格雷看到我们的最后通牒时，他会真的震惊。

sentences.en: And he is, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而他的确震惊了，对吧？

sentences.en: And he is.
sentences.zh: 他确实震惊了。

sentences.en: So that meeting that you described in your Churchill voice, Tom, 24th of July, Gray reads that out to his cabinet colleagues.
sentences.zh: 所以你用丘吉尔的嗓音描述的那次会议，汤姆，7月24日，格雷向他的内阁同僚宣读了这份文件。

sentences.en: And he says, this is the most formidable declaration I've ever seen addressed by one state to another.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是我有生以来见过一个国家向另一个国家发出的最可怕的宣言。

sentences.en: And they all say, well, the one thing we don't want to do is to get involved in a world war.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，好吧，我们最不想做的事情就是卷入一场世界大战。

sentences.en: They're absolutely adamant about that.
sentences.zh: 他们在这一点上绝对毫不妥协。

sentences.en: And they say to him, the thing to do is you go to the Germans and you go to the French.
sentences.zh: 他们对他说，现在要做的是你去跟德国人谈，再去跟法国人谈。

sentences.en: And the three of you together should be able to persuade the Austrians and the Russians not to fall out about this.
sentences.zh: 你们三方一起应该能说服奥地利人和俄国人不要为这事翻脸。

sentences.en: Now, of course, what that completely misses, they do not realize how committed the decision makers in Paris and Berlin already are.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们完全忽视了一点，那就是他们没有意识到巴黎和柏林的决策者已经陷得有多深。

sentences.en: So it's a failure of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次情报上的失败。

sentences.en: I think it is a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我想确实有点。

sentences.en: It's amazing to me that until such a late stage, Gray, perhaps misled, actually, by some of those ambassadors in London who have gone a bit native, he doesn't get that actually
sentences.zh: 令我惊奇的是，直到这么晚的阶段，格雷——实际上可能是被伦敦那些有点同化的驻在大使们所误导——他根本没有意识到其实

sentences.en: the partners for his various mediation proposals just don't actually exiSt.
sentences.zh: 他那些各种调解提议的对话伙伴根本就不存在。

sentences.en: But there is, of course, an ambassador in London who has not gone native.
sentences.zh: 但伦敦当然有一位没有被同化的大使。

sentences.en: And that is the French ambassador, Paul Cambon, who we've already mentioned.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们已经提到过的法国大使保罗·康朋。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who has been in London since 1898 as ambassador.
sentences.zh: 他自1898年以来就一直在伦敦担任大使。

sentences.en: 16 years.
But just as Gray does not speak a word of French, Paul Cambon does not speak a word of English despite having been in the country for 16 years.
sentences.zh: 但就像格雷不会说一句法语一样，尽管保罗·康朋在这个国家待了16年，他却不会说一句英语。

sentences.en: And I hugely admire that.
sentences.zh: 我极为赞赏这一点。

sentences.en: That is what I want from a French ambassador.
sentences.zh: 这正是我对法国大使的期望。

sentences.en: I mean, the amazing thing, I can't remember where I've got this from.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，神奇的是，我不记得我是从哪儿看到这个的了。

sentences.en: I think it's from Chris Clark.
sentences.zh: 我想我是从克里斯·克拉克那儿看到的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是的。

sentences.en: He's very funny about Cambon.
sentences.zh: 他对康朋的评价非常有趣。

sentences.en: During his meetings, Cambon insisted that every single utterance be translated into French, including easily recognized words such as, yes.
sentences.zh: 在会议期间，康朋坚决要求将他的每一句话都翻译成法语，包括像“是”这样容易辨认的词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So when Gray said to him, yes, this little man at the side would say, oui.
sentences.zh: 所以当格雷对他说“是”时，旁边这个矮小的家伙就会说“oui”。

sentences.en: And also his opposition to there being French schools in England on the grounds that anyone who goes to such schools are likely to grow up intellectually stunted.
sentences.zh: 还有他反对在英国设立法国学校，理由是任何去这种学校上学的人长大后智力都可能会发育不良。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And can you think of anybody, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你能想到什么人吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Can you think of anybody, a Frenchman who went to a school in England and possibly, you know, there are question marks about his acumen and maybe his life choices?
sentences.zh: 你能想到什么人吗，一个去英国上过学、而且可能，你知道的，其才智和人生选择都打上问号的法国人？

sentences.en: Theo.
sentences.zh: 特奥。

sentences.en: Poor old Theo.
sentences.zh: 可怜的老特奥。

sentences.en: And also the weird thing is that Cambon's brother, Jules, is the ambassador to Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且奇怪的是，康朋的弟弟儒勒是驻德国大使。

sentences.en: So again, it's all a kind of family affair, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这又成了一场家族事务，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they met Gray and Cambon after that cabinet meeting on the 24th of July.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在7月24日那场内阁会议之后会见了格雷和康朋。

sentences.en: And Gray said, I've dreamed up a solution to this crisis.
sentences.zh: 格雷说，我想出了一个解决这场危机的办法。

sentences.en: And it's a four power mediation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个四国调解方案。

sentences.en: So there'll be four mediators.
sentences.zh: 所以将会有四个调解国。

sentences.en: There'll be Britain, France, Germany, and Italy.
sentences.zh: 将是英国、法国、德国和意大利。

sentences.en: And between us, we can sort this out.
sentences.zh: 我们齐心协力就能把这事解决。

sentences.en: Now, there are massive problems with this idea that Gray doesn't realize.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个想法存在着格雷没有意识到的巨大问题。

sentences.en: Number one is France and Germany don't even want to do it, really.
sentences.zh: 第一点是法国和德国其实根本不想这么做。

sentences.en: They're not signed up to the idea of mediation because they are both already signed up to the idea of calling your opponents bluff and not backing down and being firm and all that
sentences.zh: 他们并不赞同调解的想法，因为他们双方都已经决定要叫板对手的虚张声势，绝不退缩，态度强硬，以及诸如此类的

sentences.en: business.
sentences.zh: 事情。

sentences.en: But also that lineup that he's described would inevitably vote 3-1 against Austria because
sentences.zh: 但同时，他所描述的这个阵营组合将不可避免地以三比一的票数反对奥地利，因为

sentences.en: Britain and France are kind of allies with Russia and Serbia.
sentences.zh: 英国和法国算是俄罗斯和塞尔维亚的盟友。

sentences.en: Germany, obviously, with Austria.
sentences.zh: 德国显然站在奥地利一边。

sentences.en: And Italy, nominally with Germany and Austria, but actually hates the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 而意大利名义上与德国和奥地利结盟，但实际上恨透了奥地利人。

sentences.en: So that is a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个问题。

sentences.en: Gray doesn't realize it, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，格雷并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And neither does Asquith, does he?
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯也没有，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because on the 24th of July, the same day that Gray is talking to Cambon, Asquith is writing in his journal, we are within measurable or imaginable distance of real Armageddon.
sentences.zh: 因为在7月24日，也就是格雷与康朋交谈的同一天，阿斯奎斯在日记中写道，我们距离真正的世界末日只有一步之遥或者可以想象的距离。

sentences.en: And the we there is Europe.
sentences.zh: 那里的“我们”指的是欧洲。

sentences.en: Happily, there seems to be no reason why we, meaning Britain, should be anything more than spectators.
sentences.zh: 令人庆幸的是，似乎没有理由让我们（意指英国）扮演除旁观者之外的任何角色。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So just on Asquith, Asquith, a great friend of the rest is history, much loved prime ministerial
sentences.zh: 说到阿斯奎斯，阿斯奎斯，他是《余下的历史》的挚友，备受喜爱的首相

sentences.en: figure, much maligned, I think, by some people at Goldhanger, Tom, very, very cruelly.
sentences.zh: 人物，我认为他遭到了戈尔德汉格某些人的恶意中伤，汤姆，极其极其残忍的中伤。

sentences.en: So Asquith, famously the kind of incarnation of the effortless superiority of the Balian man.
sentences.zh: 所以阿斯奎斯，众所周知，堪称巴力人那种不费吹灰之力的优越感的化身。

sentences.en: We know a lot about what he's thinking during this period because he's slightly letting himself down, isn't he, by, he's got a bit of a crush on his daughter's best friend.
sentences.zh: 我们对他在这一时期的想法了解很多，因为他有点自损形象，不是吗？因为他对女儿最好的朋友有点迷恋。

sentences.en: So his daughter's Violet and her best friend is called Venetia Stanley.
sentences.zh: 他的女儿叫维奥莱特，她最好的朋友叫维妮西亚·斯坦利。

sentences.en: She's 26 years old.
sentences.zh: 她26岁。

sentences.en: Asquith is 62.
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯62岁。

sentences.en: So I'm not defending it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是在为他辩护，汤姆。

sentences.en: It is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: So he's sending him all these love letters and he will often write to her.
sentences.zh: 所以他给她寄了所有这些情书，他经常写信给她。

sentences.en: I mean, he actually writes to her during cabinet meetings, which I think is probably not, not ideal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他居然在内阁会议期间给她写信，我认为这大概不太、不太合适。

sentences.en: You can't imagine Theresa May doing that.
sentences.zh: 你无法想象特雷莎·梅会那样做。

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不可能。

sentences.en: There is one recent prime minister I can imagine doing that, but let's not bring him into it.
sentences.zh: 有一个我能想象会那样做的近几年的首相，但我们还是别把他扯进来了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he says to Venetia that evening, I'm worried that Russia is trying to drag us into the war.
sentences.zh: 所以他在那天晚上对维妮西亚说，我担心俄国人正试图把我们拖入战争。

sentences.en: And he actually then goes on to say, and I think this absolutely captures the British attitude.
sentences.zh: 接着他实际上又说，我认为这绝对抓住了英国人的态度。

sentences.en: Asquith says, the curious thing is that on many, if not most of the points, Austria has a good and Serbia, a very bad case.
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯说，奇怪的是，在许多（如果不是大多数）问题上，奥地利占理，而塞尔维亚非常不占理。

sentences.en: But the Austrians are quite the stupidest people in Europe.
sentences.zh: 但奥地利人绝对是欧洲最愚蠢的人。

sentences.en: And there is a brutality of their mode of procedure, which will make most people think it's a case of a big power wantonly bullying a little one.
sentences.zh: 他们的行事方式带着一种残暴，会让大多数人觉得这是一个大国在肆意欺凌一个小国。

sentences.en: And another point, actually, he writes to her and he says, what the Serbs need is a damn good thrashing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在写给她的另一封信中还说，塞尔维亚人需要的是狠狠地挨上一顿痛打。

sentences.en: So the British are not Serbophile by any means, and they're not austrophobic.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人绝不是亲塞尔维亚派，他们也并非仇视奥地利。

sentences.en: But all they want to do is they want to see Serbia get a bit of a slap on the wrist from the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 但他们只想看到塞尔维亚被奥地利人略加惩戒。

sentences.en: So the Austrians are happy and then it all calmed down and they can go back to their fishing and he can play bridge and think about Venetia Stanley.
sentences.zh: 这样奥地利人就满意了，一切都会平息下来，他们就可以回去钓鱼，而他也可以打桥牌并想着维妮西亚·斯坦利。

sentences.en: That's basically Asquith's dream scenario.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是阿斯奎斯理想中的剧本。

sentences.en: And Grey's too, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实格雷也是这么想的。

sentences.en: I mean, Grey, unbelievably.
sentences.zh: 我是说，格雷，简直难以置信。

sentences.en: He goes off fishing, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他跑去钓鱼了，不是吗？

sentences.en: He actually goes fishing the next day.
sentences.zh: 他第二天真的去钓鱼了。

sentences.en: Yeah, tremendous behaviour.
sentences.zh: 是的，这行为真是绝了。

sentences.en: This is the day, the 25th of July, Saturday, Tom, that the ultimatum expires.
sentences.zh: 就在这一天，7月25日，星期六，汤姆，最后通牒到期了。

sentences.en: And Grey, who you might expect to stay at least in London, says, no, I'm going to go fishing.
sentences.zh: 而你可能会期望至少留在伦敦的格雷却说，不，我要去钓鱼。

sentences.en: And actually, he goes off to his country cottage, which is on the River Itchin.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他去了他在伊钦河边的乡村小屋。

sentences.en: I've seen it.
sentences.zh: 我见过的。

sentences.en: Well, this is where the most controversial person in this whole story makes his appearance, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，整个故事中最具争议的人物就是在此时登场的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because not only have you seen it, you went there with the fox-murdering anti-Brexit lawyer,
sentences.zh: 因为不仅你见过，你还是和那个虐狐的反脱欧律师一起去的，

sentences.en: Jolien Maugham.
sentences.zh: 乔利安·莫姆。

sentences.en: He's a charming man.
sentences.zh: 他是个迷人的男人。

sentences.en: Well, I don't want to lose all our listeners or our British listeners.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可不想失去我们所有的听众或者英国听众。

sentences.en: I went there with Fergal Sharkey, who's Undertones lead singer, but is also now campaigning basically against poo being dumped in our beloved rivers.
sentences.zh: 我是和弗格尔·沙基一起去的，他是“地下暗涌”乐队的主唱，现在也基本在发起反对向我们钟爱的河流倾倒粪便的运动。

sentences.en: Yeah, sewage.
sentences.zh: 对，污水。

sentences.en: Sewage is his thing.
sentences.zh: 污水就是他的主攻方向。

sentences.en: And we walked the Itchin, and he brought Jolien Maugham, who was delightful.
sentences.zh: 我们沿着伊钦河散步，他带来了乔利安·莫姆，人非常可爱。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I liked him very much.
sentences.zh: 对，我很喜欢他。

sentences.en: Oh, my word, Tom.
sentences.zh: 天哪，汤姆。

sentences.en: But Dominic, I like everyone.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，我谁都喜欢。

sentences.en: You do, you do.
sentences.zh: 你确实是，你确实是。

sentences.en: I mean, to our overseas listeners, this is just mad babble.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于我们的海外听众来说，这简直是一派胡言。

sentences.en: But British listeners can make their own minds up, as they can about other controversial characters, such as the Kaiser and other such people.
sentences.zh: 但英国听众可以自己做出判断，就像他们对其他颇具争议的人物（如德皇和其他这样的人）所做的那样。

sentences.en: Right, this is all a massive red herring.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这全都是个巨大的烟雾弹。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Germans are thinking about Gray's mediation proposal.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，德国人正在考虑格雷的调解提议。

sentences.en: So that has got back to the Kaiser, the ambassador's reporter.
sentences.zh: 所以消息已经传回给德皇了，大使也汇报了。

sentences.en: The Kaiser does not like it at all.
sentences.zh: 德皇一点也不喜欢这个提议。

sentences.en: The Kaiser scribbles on it, on the piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 德皇在上面乱涂乱画，在那张纸上。

sentences.en: He says, it's useless.
sentences.zh: 他说，这没用。

sentences.en: It's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这是胡说八道。

sentences.en: It's a complete waste of time.
sentences.zh: 这完全是浪费时间。

sentences.en: And he says, why would we betray our one friend in Europe, Austria, who we've promised that we would back?
sentences.zh: 他说，我们为什么要背叛我们在欧洲唯一的盟友奥地利呢？我们可是答应过要支持他们的。

sentences.en: Why would we suddenly say, well, actually, I think we should all have a bit of a mediation.
sentences.zh: 我们怎么会突然说，好吧，其实我觉得我们都应该进行一点调解。

sentences.en: You know, it's that classic thing of, I don't know, it's people who've fallen out and one friend says, I'll stand by you no matter what.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就那种经典的情况，我不知道，就像有些人闹翻了，其中一个朋友说，不管发生什么我都支持你。

sentences.en: Never give in to those miscrints down the road or whatever.
sentences.zh: 绝不向路上那些恶棍或其他什么人妥协。

sentences.en: And then the next day he says, actually, I was thinking, am I organising a meeting in a cafe and we can all talk?
sentences.zh: 然后第二天他又说，其实我在想，要不我在咖啡馆组织个会议，我们大家一起谈谈？

sentences.en: But what?
sentences.zh: 但什么？

sentences.en: Are you on my side or not?
sentences.zh: 你到底是站在我这边还是不站在？

sentences.en: Kaiser thinks, you can't do that to your friend.
sentences.zh: 德皇心想，你不能对你的朋友这样做。

sentences.en: I think you're revealing details about your school days here, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在这里透露了你学生时代的细节，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I'm a hold firm man, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我是个立场坚定的人，汤姆。

sentences.en: What could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么岔子呢？

sentences.en: What's the worst that could happen?
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的情况能有多坏？

sentences.en: Just a shame that your hand wasn't on the tiller of the ship of state in 1914.
sentences.zh: 只可惜1914年时掌管国家这艘船的人不是你。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Well, I wouldn't be off fishing, that's for sure, like some people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可不会去钓鱼，那是肯定的，不像某些人。

sentences.en: I wouldn't be fishing with Fox murdering lawyers.
sentences.zh: 我才不会和那些谋杀狐狸的律师一起钓鱼呢。

sentences.en: To be fair, Edward Grey wasn't either.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，爱德华·格雷也没有。

sentences.en: No, he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: He was on his own, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他当时一个人，对吧？

sentences.en: Melancholy, thinking about his wife and real tennis.
sentences.zh: 很忧郁，想着他的妻子和真网球。

sentences.en: So the Germans at this point, we're on the Saturday.
sentences.zh: 所以德国人此时此刻，我们正处于星期六。

sentences.en: The Germans still do not think that there will be a world war.
sentences.zh: 德国人仍然不认为会爆发世界大战。

sentences.en: And we know this, we can be pretty certain, because people in the Foreign Office are giving off-the-record interviews to Berlin newspapers.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点，我们可以相当确定，因为外交部的官员正在向柏林的报纸透露非官方消息。

sentences.en: Because Gottlieb van Yagov, who is the foreign minister, is talking to the editor of the Berliner
sentences.zh: 因为外交大臣戈特利布·冯·雅戈尔正在与柏林《每日导报》

sentences.en: Tageblatt, and he is saying, maybe war will come one day with Russia, and we must be firm, but it probably won't be today.
sentences.zh: 的编辑交谈，他说，也许有一天会与俄国爆发战争，我们必须坚定，但大概不会是今天。

sentences.en: His political director says the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他的政治主管也说了同样的话。

sentences.en: The Russians, they'll just shout loudly, and hot days will follow, but that will be it.
sentences.zh: 俄国人，他们只会大喊大叫，接下来会有几天热烈的情势，但也就这样了。

sentences.en: And if you're going to be critical of the Germans, as a lot of historians are, you would say, at this point, they are just being willfully reckless and self-deluding.
sentences.zh: 如果你要批评德国人，就像许多历史学家那样，你会说，在这个时候，他们只是在故意鲁莽和自欺欺人。

sentences.en: Again, it's the intelligence failure.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，这就是情报上的失败。

sentences.en: They just don't understand how seriously the Russians are taking all this.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不明白俄国人对此事的态度有多么严重。

sentences.en: Now, there are some people, particularly, I mean, there are people in the Foreign Office in London, some of Grey's Mandarins, who are a little bit more hard-nosed about this.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人，特别是，我是说，伦敦外交部里有些人，格雷的一些高级官僚，对此态度更强硬一些。

sentences.en: And the classic example of this is a man, an absolutely bizarre man, called, he has a ridiculous name, actually.
sentences.zh: 最经典的例子就是这个人，一个绝对怪异的人，叫作，他其实有个荒谬的名字。

sentences.en: What would you even call him, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你到底会怎么称呼他？

sentences.en: Sir Air Crow?
sentences.zh: 埃尔·克罗爵士吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Sir Air Crow.
sentences.zh: 埃尔·克罗爵士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now, he is the chief Germanophobe at the British Foreign Office.
sentences.zh: 现在，他是英国外交部里头号的仇德分子。

sentences.en: Despite basically being German.
sentences.zh: 尽管他基本上是个德国人。

sentences.en: Despite being German himself, which is bonkers.
sentences.zh: 尽管他自己就是德国人，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So he was born in Leipzig, educated in Dusseldorf and Berlin.
sentences.zh: 所以他出生在莱比锡，在杜塞尔多夫和柏林受过教育。

sentences.en: He first came to Britain when he was 17 to cram for the Foreign Office exam, and he spoke with a German accent.
sentences.zh: 他17岁时第一次来到英国，为外交部考试死记硬背，他说话带有德国口音。

sentences.en: One of his parents was British, which is how he qualified.
sentences.zh: 他的父母中有一位是英国人，这就是他获得资格的原因。

sentences.en: And he is fanatically anti-German.
sentences.zh: 而且他狂热地反德。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got to believe there's some strange psychological...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不得不相信这背后有什么奇怪的心理……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of Oedipal complex or something.
sentences.zh: 某种俄狄浦斯情结之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And he has been saying since 1907, oh, Germany is a bully and a brat.
sentences.zh: 他从1907年起就一直在说，哦，德国是个恃强凌弱的恶霸和小鬼。

sentences.en: It's the new boy.
sentences.zh: 它是新来的男孩。

sentences.en: It's the bullying boy at school.
sentences.zh: 它是学校里那个盛气凌人的男孩。

sentences.en: Bullies only respect strength.
sentences.zh: 恶霸只尊重实力。

sentences.en: It's reminiscent of Kipling's poem on Dengeld, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这让人想起吉卜林关于丹麦金的诗，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That, you know, you mustn't pay it.
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，你绝不能付钱。

sentences.en: You'll never get rid of the Dane.
sentences.zh: 你永远摆脱不了丹麦人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We never pay anyone Dengeld.
sentences.zh: 我们从不向任何人支付丹麦金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this weekend, Saturday the 25th of July, he writes a memo to Grey that you will see cited in every single book about this, because it really does sum up the dilemma for Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以这个周末，7月25日星期六，他给格雷写了一份备忘录，你在关于这事的每一本书里都能看到被引用，因为它确实概括了英国面临的困境。

sentences.en: He says, if there's war, he thinks there will be a war, because he says, I think the
sentences.zh: 他说，如果有战争，他认为会有一场战争，因为他说，我认为

sentences.en: Germans really do want to take over the world, because he hates Germany so much.
sentences.zh: 德国人是真的想统治世界，因为他太恨德国了。

sentences.en: And he says, if we stay out of this war, there are two alternatives.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我们置身于这场战争之外，有两种选择。

sentences.en: Number one is the Germans and the Austrians win.
sentences.zh: 第一种是德国人和奥地利人获胜。

sentences.en: And in that case, they will dominate Europe.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，他们将主宰欧洲。

sentences.en: They will dominate the channel ports, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们将主宰海峡港口，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: Our allies would have been crushed, and we'll be left alone and friendless at the mercy of the Prussians.
sentences.zh: 我们的盟友将被击溃，而我们将孤立无援、没有朋友，任由普鲁士人宰割。

sentences.en: That's number one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一种。

sentences.en: And he says, number two is the other possibility, probably less likely, the French and the Russians win.
sentences.zh: 他说，第二种是另一种可能性，可能不太大，法军和俄军获胜。

sentences.en: And he says, what would they make of us then?
sentences.zh: 他说，那他们会怎么看我们？

sentences.en: Because they would have won without us, and they would despise us for not having helped them.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在没有我们帮助的情况下赢了，他们会鄙视我们没有帮助他们。

sentences.en: And then they would turn on us.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会调转枪口对付我们。

sentences.en: They would drive us out of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他们会把我们赶出地中海。

sentences.en: They would drive us out of India.
sentences.zh: 他们会把我们赶出印度。

sentences.en: We would lose everything.
sentences.zh: 我们会失去一切。

sentences.en: And so Crow says to Grey, stop deluding yourself about your mediation and all that rubbish.
sentences.zh: 因此，克罗对格雷说，别再对你的调解和那些废话抱有幻想了。

sentences.en: You know, we should get stuck in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们应该卷起袖子加入进去。

sentences.en: We have no choice.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择。

sentences.en: Our own policy has left us the logic of our policy.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的政策把我们推向了这一政策的逻辑终点。

sentences.en: There is no debate to be had.
sentences.zh: 没什么好辩论的。

sentences.en: We should get cracking on fighting, which is obviously not what Grey wants to do.
sentences.zh: 我们应该大干一场去打仗，这显然不是格雷想做的。

sentences.en: So presumably Grey is hoping that the Serbs will maybe back down and that the whole crisis will go away?
sentences.zh: 所以大概格雷是希望塞尔维亚人或许会退缩，然后整个危机就会烟消云散？

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe.
sentences.zh: 对，也许吧。

sentences.en: Or that they will respond to the ultimatum in such a way that there'll be a fudge, maybe.
sentences.zh: 或者他们对最后通牒的回应会采取某种敷衍塞责的方式，也许吧。

sentences.en: Now, actually, let's move the focus back to Serbia.
sentences.zh: 现在，实际上，让我们把焦点重新转回塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: So Saturday is the day the ultimatum expires.
sentences.zh: 所以星期六是最后通牒到期的日子。

sentences.en: What have they been up to?
sentences.zh: 他们都在忙些什么？

sentences.en: First of all, they've been making some limited military preparations.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们一直在做一些有限的军事准备。

sentences.en: They've put the army in charge of their railways.
sentences.zh: 他们让军队接管了铁路。

sentences.en: They've started to bomb some of the bridges.
sentences.zh: 他们开始炸毁一些桥梁。

sentences.en: Well, let's just remind people, Belgrade is next to the river that constitutes the frontier with Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我们提醒大家一下，贝尔格莱德紧邻着构成奥匈帝国边界的那条河。

sentences.en: There's two rivers, actually, because the border was so different in those days, that affected the frontier, the Danube and the River Sava.
sentences.zh: 其实有两条河，因为当年的边界非常不同，这影响了边境，分别是多瑙河和萨瓦河。

sentences.en: So they are making preparations there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在那里做准备。

sentences.en: All day they've been working on a reply to the ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 一整天他们都在起草对最后通牒的回复。

sentences.en: It's one of the most famous diplomatic documents in history, and it is covered with crossings out and scribbles because they keep changing their mind about what exactly to say, and
sentences.zh: 这是历史上最著名的外交文件之一，上面涂满了划痕和乱涂乱画，因为他们不断改变主意到底该说些什么，

sentences.en: they're in a terrible panic.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了极度的恐慌之中。

sentences.en: The typewriter is jammed, so they're having to adjust it by hand.
sentences.zh: 打字机卡住了，所以他们不得不手动调整。

sentences.en: It's all a total shambles.
sentences.zh: 这一切简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: One of the key men who's drafting the reply is the trade minister, who's called Velizar
sentences.zh: 起草回复的关键人物之一是贸易大臣，名叫维利扎尔·

sentences.en: Jankovic.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇。

sentences.en: And on his mind all that day is the fact that, I mean, this tells you everything, I guess, about that kind of globalized pre-1914 world.
sentences.zh: 他那一整天脑子里想的都是，我的意思是，这说明了一切，我想，关于1914年之前的那个全球化世界。

sentences.en: His wife and children are on holiday in Austria-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子和孩子正在奥匈帝国度假。

sentences.en: They're on the Adriatic coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在亚得里亚海海岸。

sentences.en: They're in Croatia.
sentences.zh: 他们在克罗地亚。

sentences.en: So many people go to Croatia every year.
sentences.zh: 每年有那么多人去克罗地亚。

sentences.en: Well, they're there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们就在那里。

sentences.en: Because it's famous.
sentences.zh: 因为那里很有名。

sentences.en: This is an age where you don't need passports, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个不需要护照的时代，对吧？

sentences.en: Unless you're going to Russia.
sentences.zh: 除非你要去俄国。

sentences.en: You can just go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你到处都能去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确切地说。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And if you're in Serbia, the Dalmatian coast is exactly where you would go, you know, sunning yourself in Dubrovnik or whatever.
sentences.zh: 如果你在塞尔维亚，达尔马提亚海岸正是你会去的地方，你知道的，在杜布罗夫尼克晒太阳什么的。

sentences.en: And he says, oh my God, if the ultimatum expires and war comes, they will be trapped.
sentences.zh: 他说，天哪，如果最后通牒到期战争爆发，他们就被困住了。

sentences.en: And he decides, this is an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 然后他决定，这是一个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: He decides, I have to go to the German ambassador to ask him for help to get my family out.
sentences.zh: 他决定，我必须去找德国大使，请他帮忙把我的家人接出来。

sentences.en: And he says to his coachman, take me to the German embassy.
sentences.zh: 他对车夫说，带我去德国大使馆。

sentences.en: But in the general air of panic, and of course, Austria is on everybody's minds, the coachman goes to the wrong embassy.
sentences.zh: 但在普遍的恐慌气氛中，当然每个人心里都想着奥地利，车夫去错了大使馆。

sentences.en: So he arrives at the Austrian embassy at five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 所以他在五点钟到达了奥地利大使馆。

sentences.en: The ultimatum expires at six.
sentences.zh: 最后通牒在六点到期。

sentences.en: So the Austrian ambassador is waiting for a Serbian visitor.
sentences.zh: 所以奥地利大使正在等待塞尔维亚访客。

sentences.en: So he assumes this guy has come with the ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 因此他以为这个人是带着最后通牒来的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Jankovic gets out and he's like, oh, they've sent the trade minister.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇下车后心想，哦，他们把贸易大臣派来了。

sentences.en: And Jankovic, there's a terrible realization he's come to the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 而扬科维奇突然极其惊恐地意识到自己走错了地方。

sentences.en: And the Austrian ambassador is right there by the carriage saying, please step inside.
sentences.zh: 奥地利大使就站在马车旁说，请进。

sentences.en: So he steps in and then he says, I've actually come about a very embarrassing and awkward situation.
sentences.zh: 于是他走了进去，然后说，我其实是为了一件非常尴尬和棘手的情况而来的。

sentences.en: And he explains, you know, if our countries are at war, my wife and children are on the wrong side of the border.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，你知道的，如果我们两国交战，我的妻子和孩子就在国境的错误一边。

sentences.en: Well, he's basically giving away what the Serbs are going to do by saying that, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他这么说基本上就把塞尔维亚人要做的事泄露出来了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And Baron Giesel responds splendidly.
sentences.zh: 吉塞尔男爵的反应妙极了。

sentences.en: He says, again, I think the voice you're looking for here is an Austrian Roger Moore or sort of George Sanders.
sentences.zh: 他说，再说一次，我觉得你在这里寻找的声音应该是一个奥地利的罗杰·摩尔或者某种乔治·桑德斯。

sentences.en: Christopher Plummer in The Sound of Music.
sentences.zh: 《音乐之声》里的克里斯托弗·普卢默。

sentences.zh: 对，绝对是。

sentences.zh: 就是那样。

sentences.zh: 他说，作为一名绅士，我很高兴能确保您的家人获得前往威尼斯的特殊护照，我们政府将发给他们10枚金拿破仑

sentences.en: so they are not out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就不会贴钱了。

sentences.en: Do you know, Dominic, I know that this is the most disastrous failure of diplomacy in global history.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克，我知道这是全球历史上最具灾难性的外交失败。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But weirdly, I think diplomats are coming out very well from this story.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，我觉得外交官们在这个故事里表现得非常不错。

sentences.en: They're making a lot of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 他们犯了很多错误。

sentences.en: It's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 这是实话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But they're all tremendous chaps.
sentences.zh: 但他们都是了不起的家伙。

sentences.en: They're all tremendous fellows.
sentences.zh: 他们都是极好的汉子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You'd love to have a dinner party with them, wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 你一定很想请他们来开晚宴吧？

sentences.en: You really would.
sentences.zh: 真的会想。

sentences.en: Baron Giesel, Prince Lichnowski, all these characters.
sentences.zh: 吉塞尔男爵、利希诺夫斯基亲王，所有这些大人物。

sentences.en: Probably not the French guy because, you know, I don't want to see his translator.
sentences.zh: 大概不会请那个法国人，因为，你知道的，我可不想看他的翻译。

sentences.en: So as Jankovic leaves, it occurs to him, the Baron is in his traveling clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以，当扬科维奇离开时，他突然意识到，男爵穿着旅行装。

sentences.en: He's wearing plus fours.
sentences.zh: 他穿着灯笼裤。

sentences.en: Everything is packed up, ready to go, ready for war.
sentences.zh: 一切都打包好了，准备出发，准备开战。

sentences.en: And he realizes, you know, there is no way the Austrians are not going to fight.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，奥地利人是不可能不打这一仗的。

sentences.en: And indeed, with five minutes to go until the deadline, 5.55, the Prime Minister Nikola
sentences.zh: 果不其然，在距离最后期限还有五分钟、也就是五点五十五分时，首相尼古拉

sentences.en: Pazic arrives at the Austrian legation.
sentences.zh: 帕希奇抵达了奥地利公使馆。

sentences.en: Giesel throws him into the study and Pazic says, part of your demands we have accepted.
sentences.zh: 吉塞尔把他拉进书房，帕希奇说，你们的部分要求我们已经接受了。

sentences.en: For the rest, we place our hope in the loyalty and chivalry of an Austrian general.
sentences.zh: 至于其余部分，我们寄希望于一位奥地利将军的忠诚与骑士精神。

sentences.en: And he gives him the reply to the note.
sentences.zh: 接着他把对最后通牒的回复交给了对方。

sentences.en: And to cut a long story short, the reply to the note, it's often misconstrued.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，对这份最后通牒的回复，常常被人们误解。

sentences.en: People say the Serbs accepted all the demands except the most inflammatory number six.
sentences.zh: 人们说塞尔维亚人接受了所有的要求，除了最具煽动性的第六条。

sentences.en: That's actually not right.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And that's the one where the Habsburgs demand the right to join the investigation on Serbian soil.
sentences.zh: 那是哈布斯堡王朝要求有权在塞尔维亚领土上参与调查的那一条。

sentences.en: But that's not right.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They accepted all the demands in theory, but not in practice.
sentences.zh: 他们在理论上接受了所有要求，但在实践中却没有。

sentences.en: With caveats.
sentences.zh: 带有附加条件。

sentences.en: There were always caveats.
sentences.zh: 总是有各种附加条件。

sentences.en: They said, well, we don't think this nationalist organization even exists, but if you can prove it exists, we'll help you to shut it down.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，我们认为这个民族主义组织甚至都不存在，但如果你能证明它存在，我们会帮你取缔它。

sentences.en: Or they say, yes, we will do this insofar as it is commensurate with international law.
sentences.zh: 或者他们说，是的，我们会在符合国际法的范围内这样做。

sentences.en: So when Giesel looks at the document, he says, I mean, he wrote later, nearly all our demands were twisted, robbed of their meaning and purpose.
sentences.zh: 所以当吉塞尔看到这份文件时，他说，我的意思是，他后来写道，我们几乎所有的要求都被曲解了，被剥夺了原本的意义和目的。

sentences.en: And their fulfillment, if not directly refused, was so hedged in reservations that it was in practice useless.
sentences.zh: 而它们的兑现，即使没有被直接拒绝，也被重重保留条件所限制，以至于在实践中毫无用处。

sentences.en: And all diplomatic historians, by the way, this isn't an anti-Serbian thing.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，所有的外交史学家都认为——这不是针对塞尔维亚的偏见——

sentences.en: All diplomatic historians have said it was a brilliantly, brilliantly written reply that basically gave the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 所有的外交史学家都说过，这是一份极其精妙、极其高明的手稿，基本上给了奥地利人……

sentences.en: Seemed to give them almost everything, but in reality gave them absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 似乎给了他们几乎一切，但实际上什么也没给。

sentences.en: And Giesel reads it and he says, fine, it's absolutely clear.
sentences.zh: 吉塞尔看完后说，好吧，这下完全清楚了。

sentences.en: He said, I had nothing to weigh, nothing to decide.
sentences.zh: 他说，我没什么可权衡的，也没什么好决定的。

sentences.en: All there was to do was to leave.
sentences.zh: 唯一要做的就是离开。

sentences.en: So he burns the ciphers.
sentences.zh: 于是他烧毁了密码本。

sentences.en: He literally locks the embassy and gives the key to the Germans.
sentences.zh: 他甚至直接锁上了大使馆，把钥匙交给了德国人。

sentences.en: Please look after the embassy.
sentences.zh: 请帮忙照看下大使馆。

sentences.en: And then he goes to the station.
sentences.zh: 然后他去了火车站。

sentences.en: And you were saying about diplomats, Tom, all the other diplomats, all the other ambassadors
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到外交官，汤姆，所有其他的外交官、所有其他的大使

sentences.en: have assembled at the station to see him off, waving their top hats and stuff, except for the Russians.
sentences.zh: 都聚集在火车站为他送行，挥舞着大礼帽之类的东西，除了俄国人。

sentences.en: And I suppose you'd say understandably.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说这是情有可原的。

sentences.en: The French, I think they could have tried.
sentences.zh: 法国人嘛，我觉得他们本可以试着去送送。

sentences.en: And the Romanians, who are trying to get into bed with the Russians and the French, I think they could have made a showing as well.
sentences.zh: 还有罗马尼亚人，他们正试图巴结俄国人和法国人，我觉得他们也本该露个面。

sentences.en: I think that was poor.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这做得挺逊的。

sentences.en: Well, I'm afraid that reflects badly on all three.
sentences.zh: 好吧，恐怕这让这三方都很没面子。

sentences.en: All three, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实是这三方。

sentences.en: You were saying how close it is.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说到这有多近。

sentences.en: It took him 10 minutes to get the train and then to cross the bridge into Austrian territory.
sentences.zh: 他坐火车只花了十分钟，然后就穿过桥梁进入了奥地利领土。

sentences.en: That's how close they are.
sentences.zh: 他们就是离得这么近。

sentences.en: The news reaches Vienna very quickly, of course.
sentences.zh: 消息当然很快传到了维也纳。

sentences.en: And there are huge crowds outside the war ministry.
sentences.zh: 战争部外面聚集了庞大的人群。

sentences.en: There are people singing patriotic songs.
sentences.zh: 人们在唱着爱国歌曲。

sentences.en: They're singing this famous anthem about the siege of Belgrade in 1717.
sentences.zh: 他们在唱那首关于1717年贝尔格莱德围城战的著名赞美诗。

sentences.en: They're waving flags, great crowds of students.
sentences.zh: 他们挥舞着旗帜，成群结队的大学生聚集在一起。

sentences.en: We should sacrifice everything for our emperor.
sentences.zh: 我们应该为我们的皇帝牺牲一切。

sentences.en: There is genuine excitement in Austria.
sentences.zh: 奥地利上下洋溢着真正的兴奋之情。

sentences.en: And this is what gives people the sense that everyone greeted the war with great enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们会觉得所有人都是以极大的热情来迎接这场战争的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But it's kind of surface wrath to a degree, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这只是一种表面的狂热，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's surface.
sentences.zh: 只是表面现象。

sentences.en: And of course, don't forget the Austrians, they think they're only fighting Serbia.
sentences.zh: 当然，别忘了奥地利人以为他们只是在和塞尔维亚打仗。

sentences.en: I mean, as it happens, their campaign in Serbia is a total disaster.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上，他们在塞尔维亚的军事行动是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: But it's a slightly different issue.
sentences.zh: 但这又是另一个话题了。

sentences.en: A small Balkan war.
sentences.zh: 一场小型的巴尔干战争。

sentences.en: And they're not celebrating a world war.
sentences.zh: 他们庆祝的不是一场世界大战。

sentences.en: They're celebrating revenge for their archduke, as they sit.
sentences.zh: 如他们所说，他们是在为他们的王储复仇而庆祝。

sentences.en: However, there is one person who doesn't react in quite that way.
sentences.zh: 然而，有一个人的反应并不完全是这样。

sentences.en: The emperor, Franz Josef, is in Bad Ischel on the lakeside at his summer house with Count
sentences.zh: 皇帝弗兰茨·约瑟夫正身处湖畔的巴德伊舍，和外交大臣贝希特尔多夫伯爵一起

sentences.en: Berktold, the foreign minister.
sentences.zh: 待在他的避暑山庄里。

sentences.en: And they're waiting for the news.
sentences.zh: 他们在等待消息。

sentences.en: And an aide comes in to tell Franz Josef the news and says the ultimatum expired.
sentences.zh: 一名随从进来向弗兰茨·约瑟夫汇报消息，说最后通牒已经到期。

sentences.en: You know, relations have been severed, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，外交关系已经断绝，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Franz Josef just is totally quiet and still.
sentences.zh: 而弗兰茨·约瑟夫只是异常安静和镇定。

sentences.en: And he just says, also doch.
sentences.zh: 他只是说道：“终究还是来了。”

sentences.en: Well, then, there it is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然如此，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: And there it is.
sentences.zh: 那就这样吧。

sentences.en: The states of Europe, tethered together by a mountaineer's rope, getting ready to vanish over the precipice into the abyss, Dominic, of war.
sentences.zh: 欧洲各国被登山绳紧紧栓在一起，正准备跌落深渊，投入多米尼克所说的战争的万丈深渊。

sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想继续关注，我们这个系列还有最后两集。

sentences.zh: 它们将在适的时候发布。
